ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Given the figure, draw CE$\perp$BE at point E, BF$\perp$CF at point F, and AG$\perp$DG at point G,\\
thus $\angle$BEC=$\angle$CFD=$\angle$AGD=$90^\circ$,\\
thus BE$\parallel$CF$\parallel$DG,\\
thus $\angle$B=$\angle$FCD=$\angle$ADG,\\
thus $\triangle$BEC$\sim$ $\triangle$CFD$\sim$ $\triangle$DGA,\\
thus BC$\colon$ CD$\colon$ AD=EC$\colon$ FD$\colon$ GA=1$\colon$ 3$\colon$ 2.\\

ready3_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, $A$ and $B$ are located on the horizontal lines of the circular grid. Points $C$ and $D$ are the intersections of the diameter $AB$ with the grid lines. What is the ratio of $BC:CD:DA$?
ready3_open_rewrite.raw_answer: \textbf{Solution:} Given the figure, draw $CE\perp BE$ at point $E$, $BF\perp CF$ at point $F$, and $AG\perp DG$ at point $G$. Thus $\angle BEC=\angle CFD=\angle AGD=90^\circ$. Thus $BE\parallel CF\parallel DG$. Thus $\angle B=\angle FCD=\angle ADG$. Thus $\triangle BEC\sim\triangle CFD\sim\triangle DGA$. Therefore, $BC:CD:AD=EC:FD:GA=1:3:2$, so the answer is $\boxed{1:3:2}$.

ready3_open_rewrite.final_cot:
Image description: The figure is a circular grid, with multiple equally spaced horizontal grid lines and approximately vertical grid lines inside. A slanted line segment AB passes near the center of the circle and is the diameter of the circle. A is on a horizontal grid line near the circumference in the lower left, and B is on a horizontal grid line near the circumference in the upper right. The slanted line AB intersects the middle horizontal grid lines to form points C and D, where C is located in the upper area near B, and D is located in the lower area near A. Looking along the slanted diameter from B toward A, the vertical grid height difference from B to C is 1 grid interval, the vertical grid height difference from C to D is 3 grid intervals, and the vertical grid height difference from D to A is 2 grid intervals.

Reasoning: Construct auxiliary right triangles for BC, CD, and DA respectively, so that the hypotenuse of each triangle is on the same slanted diameter AB, and one leg represents the corresponding vertical grid height difference. Since these horizontal grid lines are parallel to each other, and the three hypotenuse segments are all on the same straight line AB, the three right triangles have the same acute angle, so they are similar. In similar triangles, the corresponding hypotenuse lengths are proportional to the corresponding vertical heights. Therefore BC:CD:DA equals the ratio of their corresponding vertical grid height differences, namely 1:3:2.
